slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Gen 9:26-27: Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem! May Canaan be the servant of Shem. May God expand the territory of Japheth; may he dwell in the tents of Shem.
slides.body: “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem! May Canaan be the servant of Shem. May God expand the territory of Japheth; may he dwell in the tents of Shem.”
slides.heading: Gen 9:26-27

slides.alt_text: Slide 2: Did God become Shem’s descendant? Noah calls the LORD “the God of Shem.” Luke later lists Shem among Jesus’s ancestors. Some Christians combine these facts into a prediction that God would join Shem’s family.
slides.body: Noah calls the LORD “the God of Shem.” Luke later lists Shem among Jesus’s ancestors. Some Christians combine these facts into a prediction that God would join Shem’s family.
slides.heading: Did God become Shem’s descendant?

slides.alt_text: Slide 3: Why Christians connect them Shem’s family line leads to Abraham, Israel and eventually Jesus. The next verse may also picture God living among Shem’s people. For Christians who believe Jesus is God, those details can feel significant.
slides.body: Shem’s family line leads to Abraham, Israel and eventually Jesus. The next verse may also picture God living among Shem’s people. For Christians who believe Jesus is God, those details can feel significant.
slides.heading: Why Christians connect them

slides.alt_text: Slide 4: But that isn’t what Noah says Noah says the LORD is Shem’s God. He never says God will be born as one of Shem’s descendants. Luke supplies Jesus’s family tree, but does not say Noah predicted it.
slides.body: Noah says the LORD is Shem’s God. He never says God will be born as one of Shem’s descendants. Luke supplies Jesus’s family tree, but does not say Noah predicted it.
slides.heading: But that isn’t what Noah says

title: Does Noah predict that God will become Shem's descendant?
